prompt: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “College provides a great opportunity for students to explore various possibilities and find the right path for themselves.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
first: College provides a great opportunity for students to explore various possibilities and find the right path for themselves.
body: College provides a great opportunity for students to explore various possibilities and find the right path for themselves. Unlike high school, where most of their time is devoted to preparing for exams, college offers a wide range of courses, clubs and activities, along with much more free time.

Making good use of this opportunity requires an open mind. Students can take elective courses outside their major, join clubs that interest them or do internships in different fields. Through such attempts, they gradually discover what they are good at and what they truly enjoy. My roommate, for example, majored in chemistry but found during a volunteer teaching program that he loved working with children. He later decided to pursue a career in education and has never been happier. Even an attempt that does not work out is valuable, because it shows students which path is not for them.

Of course, exploration should not become aimless wandering. Students need to reflect on their experiences regularly and narrow down their choices. By combining bold exploration with careful reflection, they can make the most of their college years and find a path that really suits them.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
first: Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth.
body: Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth. With smartphones, online games and countless other distractions within easy reach, students who lack self-control can easily waste their precious time and fall behind in their studies.

Self-discipline contributes to growth in several ways. To begin with, it is the key to academic success. Students who stick to a regular study schedule tend to learn more efficiently and perform better than those who rely on last-minute cramming. Furthermore, self-discipline benefits physical and mental health. Going to bed on time, exercising regularly and eating sensibly keep us energetic and in a good mood. Most importantly, it builds character. Each time we resist a temptation or finish a dull but necessary task, we become a little stronger and more reliable.

Developing self-discipline, however, takes time. Students can start by setting small, specific goals, such as getting up at seven every morning or reading for thirty minutes a day, and sticking to them until they become habits. Keeping a daily record of their progress can also help. Once self-discipline becomes part of their character, students will find it much easier to turn their goals into achievements.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
first: To increase the likelihood of success, one should set realistic goals and work persistently towards them.
body: To increase the likelihood of success, one should set realistic goals and work persistently towards them. Many people fail not because they lack ability, but because their goals are either unrealistic or abandoned halfway.

A realistic goal is one that matches our abilities and circumstances. If a goal is set too high, repeated failure may soon destroy our confidence; if it is too low, it offers little motivation. A student preparing for CET-6, for example, would do better to set a target of learning twenty new words a day than to try to memorize a whole dictionary in a month. However, a sensible goal alone is not enough. Success also depends on persistent effort, especially when progress seems slow. Just as dripping water wears away a stone, small steps taken every day eventually add up to great achievements.

Therefore, we should first assess our strengths and weaknesses honestly and set goals that are challenging but achievable. Then we must stick to our plans day after day, adjusting our methods when necessary but never giving up easily. Realistic goals combined with persistent effort will greatly increase our chances of success in any field.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. (You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.)
first: There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today’s world.
body: There is a growing awareness of the importance of digital literacy and skills in today’s world. From online shopping and mobile payments to remote work and virtual classes, digital technology has become part of almost every aspect of our lives.

Digital literacy matters for several reasons. First, it is essential for study and work. Students need it to find reliable materials and use learning platforms, while employees increasingly rely on digital tools to communicate and solve problems. Second, it helps keep us safe online. People with good digital literacy can recognize fraud, protect their personal information and tell trustworthy sources from misleading ones. Third, it allows everyone to share the benefits of technological progress. Without basic digital skills, for instance, many elderly people feel left behind because they cannot book a doctor’s appointment or buy a train ticket online.

To improve digital literacy, schools should offer courses on information skills and online safety, and communities can organize training sessions for elderly residents who struggle with smartphones. As individuals, we should keep learning new digital skills while using technology wisely. That is how we can truly benefit from the digital age instead of being overwhelmed by it.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. (You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.)
first: Nowadays more and more college students have come to realize social practice and academic learning are equally important.
body: Nowadays more and more college students have come to realize social practice and academic learning are equally important. Knowledge from textbooks lays the foundation for our abilities, while hands-on experience turns that knowledge into real skills.

On the one hand, academic learning is indispensable. Without a solid grasp of theories and methods, social practice would lack direction and achieve little. On the other hand, social practice deepens and tests what we have learned. When students take part in internships, field research or volunteer programs, they not only apply their knowledge to real problems but also develop communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills that classrooms alone can hardly provide. Last summer, several agriculture majors in my class spent a month helping farmers in a village improve their crops, and they came back with a much deeper understanding of what they had learned in class.

Therefore, college students should strike a balance between the two. Neither should be sacrificed for the other. They should study hard in class while seizing every opportunity to gain practical experience, so that theory and practice can reinforce each other. Students who do so will grow into well-rounded graduates ready to serve society.

You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. (You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.)
first: Nowadays, cultivating independent learning ability is becoming increasingly crucial for personal development.
body: Nowadays, cultivating independent learning ability is becoming increasingly crucial for personal development. In an age when knowledge is updated at an astonishing speed, what we learn at school can hardly meet all our needs in life.

Independent learning ability brings many benefits. First, it enables us to keep up with the times. Whenever we face a new field or a new technology, we can find the right materials, make a plan and master it on our own. Second, it fosters critical thinking. Instead of passively accepting what teachers say, independent learners ask questions, compare different views and form their own judgments. Third, it builds confidence. Many working adults, for example, have taught themselves programming through online courses and successfully changed careers. Such experiences convince people that they can learn almost anything they set their minds to.

To cultivate this ability, students should learn to set their own goals, manage their time and reflect on their progress regularly. Teachers should guide their students rather than spoon-feed them, leaving them room to explore and make discoveries of their own. With the ability to learn independently, we can keep growing throughout our lives.
